narrative.overview: everydaytool is a persistent desktop tool launcher, not a monitoring dashboard. A narrow transparent rail keeps tools within one click; the center displays the active workspace while tools opened in this session stay mounted until closed. Translucent content surfaces establish spatial layering, fine rules establish structure, and signal blue marks action, selection and focus. Decoration never creates hierarchy.
keyCharacteristics: Tools first, status second; the home screen keeps only a lightweight running dot and label, without versions or category metadata.
Opened tools stay mounted while switching; closing a tool unmounts it and releases its timers, subscriptions, webviews and tool-level backend sessions.
48px transparent rail and 48px transparent topbar at equal width and height, plus a single 16px glass work surface.
Cool glass, pale blue ambient light and 1px translucent edges, without stacked cards or heavy shadows.
Brand blue #3390ec and ink blue #006dc3 are the only accent colors.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Only brand blue carries action, current selection and focus. Everything else emphasizes through scale, space and neutral value.

rules.name: The Neutral Label Rule
rules.body: Selected rows and active rail labels use neutral primary text, not bright blue small type.

rules.name: The Glass Boundary Rule
rules.body: Glass belongs to surface-to-background boundaries only. Fields, rows, buttons and fills never add backdrop-filter.

rules.name: The Content Is Opaque Rule
rules.body: Text, icons, status dots, progress and switch knobs remain opaque. Transparency belongs to large surfaces.

rules.name: The No Micro Type Rule
rules.body: Production UI never uses 9–10px text. The minimum size is 11px, including table headers, status lines and keycaps.

rules.name: The One Display Size Rule
rules.body: 25px is reserved for the home title. Tool titles are 17px and section titles 16px.

dos: Do keep exactly one primary work surface per tool.
Do move settings, diagnostics, help and installation into an inspector, drawer or sub-route.
Do keep each home tool row to icon, name, one-line description, running state and pin.
Do expose every tool through Ctrl/Cmd+K and the left rail.
Do verify text contrast on every material and in night glass.
Do confirm only real unfinished work before closing; release everything else immediately.
donts: Don't show versions, categories, processes, paths or statistics on the home screen.
Don't stack UiPanel cards as the first viewport of a tool.
Don't use cross-tool KeepAlive instead of ToolPane's explicit persistence; closing a tool must unmount it.
Don't give tools separate accent colors.
Don't use 9–10px text, bright blue small type, colored side stripes or gradient text.
Don't apply backdrop-filter or shadows to every layer.
Don't use a modal for work that belongs inline in the workspace.
